newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: EU must wait on Yugo trade perks - Kosovo leader.
newsitem.headline: EU must wait on Yugo trade perks - Kosovo leader.

text.p: Kosovo Albanian leader Ibrahim Rugova has appealed to the European Union not to grant economic and trade preferentials to Yugoslavia before the question of Serbia's mostly Albanian province is resolved.

In a letter on Monday to the chairman of the EU Council of Foreign Ministers, Hans Van Mierlo of the Netherlands, Rugova said the problem of Kosovo "must be resolved in harmony with the political will of the people of Kosova".
Rugova, who heads the biggest ethnic Albanian party the Democratic League of Kosova, said the resolution of the Kosovo question is the key factor for preserving peace and stability in the region.

Rugova said the overall situation in Kosovo continues to be "repressive, grave and dangerous" due to the Serbian regime's practices against majority Albanians, who outnumber Serbs nine to one in the southern province.
Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic rescinded Kosovo's autonomy in 1989, claiming ethnic Albanians wanted to secede to create a Greater Albania.
EU foreign ministers are to discuss restoring Yugoslavia's trade privileges at a meeting in Luxembourg on Tuesday.
The ministers will link implementation of trade preferences to respect of human rights and tolerance of opposition groups.
Trade concessions were abolished in 1991 punishing Belgrade for its role in the wars which led to the breakup of the former Yugoslav federation.

A U.N. trade embargo imposed in 1992 on Serbia and Montenegro, comprising the new Yugoslavia, was formally lifted last October but an "outer wall" of sanctions remained barring the country's full return to the world community.

Removal of the outer wall is conditional on Yugoslavia's respect of human rights in Kosovo, cooperation with The Hague War Crimes Tribunal and progress in talks on division of former Yugoslavia's assets with other ex-Yugoslav republics.
